questions.question: Describe where South Africa's main minerals are mined.
questions.expected_answer: Gold is mined in the Witwatersrand Basin, an arc through Gauteng, North West and the Free State. Coal is mined mainly in Mpumalanga. Platinum is mined around Rustenburg and in Limpopo. Diamonds have been mined around Kimberley, at Cullinan and on the west coast. Iron ore and manganese are mined in the Northern Cape, copper at Phalaborwa, and heavy minerals near Richards Bay.

questions.question: How do you read and describe a mining map?
questions.expected_answer: First read the key, which explains the symbols, such as a yellow triangle for gold or a black square for coal. Then find the symbols on the map and describe where they are using provinces, towns and compass directions. Look for patterns, such as most mining being in the north and north-east, and look at railways to see how minerals are moved.

questions.question: Explain how mining has shaped settlement in South Africa.
questions.expected_answer: Many towns began as mining settlements: Johannesburg grew after gold was found in 1886, Kimberley because of diamonds, eMalahleni because of coal, Rustenburg because of platinum and Welkom because of gold. Mines attract factories, shops, schools, roads and people looking for work. When a mine closes, a town can shrink, like Pilgrim's Rest, which is now a museum town.
